entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Gaius Fabius Ambustus was a Roman consul in 358 BC, who played a pivotal role in the Roman Republic's response to the Gaulish threat. As Interrex in 355 BC, he was appointed dictator through fear of the Gauls, marking a turning point in the Roman Republic's relationship with its northern neighbors.

This event had significant consequences for the Roman Republic, as it led to the expansion of Roman influence in the Mediterranean and the development of a more centralized government. The appointment of a dictator also marked a shift away from the traditional Roman system of governance, which emphasized the role of the Senate and the people.

The legacy of Gaius Fabius Ambustus can be seen in the Roman Republic's continued expansion and the development of its military tactics, which became a model for future Roman leaders. The appointment of a dictator also set a precedent for future Roman leaders, who would use this power to shape the course of Roman history.

The impact of this event can be seen in the many Roman monuments and buildings that were constructed during this period, including the temple of Jupiter on the Capitoline Hill.
